artigo.texto: Data centers and artificial intelligence may not rank among voters’ top concerns heading into the midterms, but growing anxiety over their effect on electricity bills and local communities is giving Democrats and allied groups an opening to connect the industry’s rapid expansion to the issue that has consistently dominated the campaign: the cost of living. The League of Conservation Voters Victory Fund, a Democratic-aligned super PAC, launched a $2 million digital ad campaign Tuesday targeting six Republican House incumbents over their support for H.R. 1 (known as the “One Big Beautiful Bill”), President Donald Trump’s signature tax-and-spending law. The group is seeking to link the lawmakers to tax benefits received by companies involved in the data center boom. The ads will target Reps. Juan Ciscomani of Arizona, Zach Nunn of Iowa, Brad Finstad of Minnesota, Tom Barrett of Michigan, Derrick Van Orden of Wisconsin and Rob Wittman of Virginia. The ads will run through Election Day, with 46% of the buy going to connected television, 43% to YouTube and 10% to social media. All six districts are among those the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee has identified as potential pickup opportunities in November, which the committee refers to as “red to blue” districts. The campaign represents an effort by the environmental group to capitalize on a political backlash that has increasingly followed proposed data centers across the country. Residents in communities facing new developments have raised concerns about electricity costs, water use, noise and strain on local power grids. The issue has drawn attention from both parties: The House overwhelmingly passed legislation last week directing state utility regulators to consider whether data centers and other large electricity users should shoulder infrastructure costs associated with their power demands. LCV Victory Fund is betting that those local concerns can be tied to the broader affordability debate. “These six districts have planned or operational data centers in their districts,” Sara Schreiber, senior vice president of LCV Victory Fund, told MS NOW. “All of these members voted for the $80 billion in tax breaks for these companies.” The ads use what the group describes as “a tongue-in-cheek ’90’s Infomercial style” to make that argument. For example, in the Michigan spot targeting Barrett (embedded above), a narrator asks viewers, “Is your neighborhood too quiet? Is your water too clean? Paying too little for electricity?” before accusing Barrett of taking “data center money” and supporting tax breaks benefiting the industry. Barrett, however, has also sought to position himself against unchecked data center development. In August, he introduced two bills that his office said were designed to preserve local control over whether data centers are built and to prevent the federal government from overriding local zoning decisions. Barrett said residents in mid-Michigan had raised concerns about the projects’ potential effects on utility bills, land and water. “People in mid-Michigan are tired of big corporations and politicians negotiating backroom deals to put data centers in our communities without hearing from the people who would be impacted the most,” Barrett wrote at the time. But even his decision to introduce the legislation underscores how the issue has gained political traction. The $80 billion figure cited by LCV Victory Fund requires some context. An August analysis by the Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy, or ITEP, found that six large companies — Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, JPMorgan Chase and Nvidia — received a combined $83 billion in federal income tax breaks in 2025. However, ITEP’s analysis did not attribute all $83 billion to tax breaks specifically for data centers. ITEP describes itself as a “non-profit, non-partisan tax policy organization” that promotes “tax justice.”

artigo.texto: The News Amazonâs chief sustainability officer said Tuesday the company needed to âdo betterâ on communicating the environmental impact of its vast data center buildout, amid growing opposition to the projects in the US and Europe. âThere is a lot of debate, backlash against data centers in this country right now, and one of the things that weâre doing is taking a look at what have we done well and where have we fallen down and what do we need to do better,â Kara Hurst told Semaforâs The Next Three Billion event in New York. âAnd so, weâre revising a number of our practices. Weâre calling for a lot more transparency and accountability because thatâs what people in these communities deserve. Weâre saying, âhold us accountable for our practices,ââ Hurst said. Amazonâs carbon footprint grew for the second year in a row in 2025, as the tech giant accelerated its data center buildout, investing $220 billion in capital expenditure in 2026 alone. But local opposition threatens to hinder tech giantsâ race to build, with data center projects worth some $68 billion delayed or blocked because of local opposition between April and June this year, according to Data Center Watch. Amazon is looking to publish more metrics tracking its environmental footprint such as the effectiveness of energy and water usage at sites, Hurst said, part of a wider effort to address concerns from environmentalists and communities. Communities where data centers are built should also get a âreturn on that investment,â Hurst said. âThey should get workforce development, they should get upskilling, they should get economic development.â Know More There is currently no national framework in the US requiring hyperscalers to report data centersâ environmental impact. But Hurst said that voluntary reporting has an advantage over mandated disclosure: It lets companies put data out, have scientists test whether the metrics hold up, and revise the methodology if they donât, rather than locking in a potentially flawed standard. âWhat we need is to publish data, information thatâs science-led, and to publish it quickly and to put it out there and say, âIs this the right methodology?ââ she said. The data center race has posed a dilemma for sustainability goals globally. An S&P Global assessment of data center companies globally found that just 15 of the 50 firms surveyed received a passing grade signaling that they would be low-carbon and climate-resilient by 2030. Amazon has set a goal to be net-zero carbon by 2040, but Hurst said the firm will likely see emissions rise in the near term as the data center buildout heats up. âWeâve said all along this is not going to be linear,â Hurst said.

artigo.texto: Publicidade A demanda por data centers provocada pela inteligência artificial e a computação em nuvem já vinha acelerando o crescimento da Ascenty nos últimos anos. Mas a aprovação do Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata) leva as projeções a um novo nível. Em três anos, a companhia, uma das líderes do setor no Brasil, deve quadruplicar de tamanho. Maior exemplo do ciclo de crescimento aguardado pela companhia é o projeto de um novo data center em Sumaré, no interior de São Paulo. Com investimento de US$ 1 bilhão, o espaço foi projetado para atender a apenas um hyperscaler, o nome dado a gigantes do processamento e armazenamento em nuvem, como Google (GOGL34) , Amazon (AMZO34) e Microsoft (MSFT34). A informação de quem ocupará o espaço é confidencial. O que dá para saber é que este é apenas um dos diversos projetos que devem levar a Ascenty ao patamar de 1 gigawatt em potência dedicada exclusivamente aos seus data centers em três anos, algo que ocupará aproximadamente 1 milhão de metros quadrados em novos data centers. “O grande empecilho do Brasil não era energia, era o custo de operar aqui versus o custo de operar lá fora”, conta o CEO da Ascenty, Christopher Torto, ao InfoMoney. Sua avaliação é de que o mercado local seguiria crescendo em um ritmo acelerado, mas os incentivos tributários do Redata devem promover um salto de investimentos. Sancionado pelo presidente Lula na última semana, o regime tributário isenta empresas que instalarem data centers no Brasil de PIS/Pasep, Cofins e IPI na aquisição de equipamentos de tecnologia da informação e computação, importados ou produzidos no Brasil, destinados à implantação, modernização e ampliação desses empreendimentos. Como contou o InfoMoney, companhias como a Nvidia, principal fornecedora dos chips de última geração para treinamento de inteligência artificial, já projetam que o Brasil deve levar os custos de implementação de projetos no país a patamares competitivos com os principais mercados do mundo. Continua depois da publicidade “Vamos começar a ver nos próximos seis meses anúncios de projetos com contratos. Infelizmente, muitos data centers hoje anunciam projetos, mas não têm clientes”, aponta o executivo. Para o executivo, embora o mercado brasileiro dê sinais do seu potencial, ainda há muitos projetos especulativos sem investimento contratado. Além da demanda, novos projetos da Ascenty também têm sido impulsionados pela necessidade de atualização do parque de servidores no país. Acontece que os racks que comportam as GPUs para processar IA se tornaram cada vez mais pesados conforme o tamanho dos chips diminuiu. Para se ter ideia, em alguns projetos esses servidores chegam a consumir 210 quilowatts, contra 8 quilowatts em racks dedicados a serviços de nuvem tradicionais. Continua depois da publicidade O primeiro efeito: os novos racks são mais pesados e precisam de estruturas mais resistentes para suportá-los no piso. Além do mais, os equipamentos mais modernos dissipam ainda mais calor que suas versões tradicionais, exigindo a adequação da refrigeração por ar para a refrigeração líquida, explica Torto. Toda essa estrutura demanda energia. Embora hoje o país gere mais energia do que consome, o mercado vê alguns gargalos na transmissão: “A partir de 2029 não vai ser um problema tão grande porque há muito reforço das linhas de transmissão agora. Governo, Anatel e ONS estão olhando para isso, tentando trazer investimentos mais rápido”, afirma o executivo da Ascenty.

artigo.texto: Camel Group 12V Sodium-Ion Battery Selected for European OEM Pre-Development Project WUHAN, China, Aug. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Camel Group Co., Ltd. (Shanghai Stock Exchange: 601311.SH) announced that its 12V sodium-ion battery business has been selected for a pre-development project with a major European automotive manufacturer, bringing the company’s sodium-ion battery technology into the OEM’s technology development and validation process for next-generation low-voltage applications. The project builds on Camel Group’s engineering development of cylindrical sodium-ion battery samples and its small-batch production capabilities for sodium-ion battery products. It follows the adoption of Camel Group’s 12V lithium-ion batteries by major European automakers and represents another step in the company’s overseas R&D collaboration in next-generation low-voltage battery technology. Sodium-ion batteries are attracting increasing attention in automotive applications as manufacturers explore alternative technologies for evolving vehicle electrical architectures. Their resource availability, low-temperature performance and cycle-life potential make sodium-ion technology a potential option for automotive low-voltage battery systems, particularly amid evolving battery regulations and decarbonization requirements. Camel Group has more than four decades of experience in low-voltage batteries, with a product portfolio spanning conventional lead-acid, EFB, AGM, 12V lithium-ion and 12V sodium-ion batteries. In sodium-ion technology, the company has completed the engineering development of cylindrical battery samples and established small-batch production capabilities. Camel Group is also the lead proposing organization for the international standard proposal 12 V Sodium-ion Batteries for Automotive Start-Stop Applications. The proposal was unanimously approved by IEC/TC21 and has formally entered the international standardization process. The European OEM project provides an opportunity for further validation of Camel Group’s sodium-ion battery technology and product adaptability under European automotive requirements. Camel Group will continue to advance sodium-ion battery technology and deepen collaborative R&D with automotive manufacturers in China and overseas markets, developing low-voltage battery solutions focused on safety, adaptability and stable performance under diverse operating conditions. artigo.texto: 2 min leitura Sunenergy reforça sustentabilidade de instalação solar com bateria industrial A instalação solar passa agora a armazenar excedentes de energia produzida no período de almoço e aos fins de semana, evitando o seu desperdício. 23 Set 2026 - 12:42 2 min leitura A Sunenergy, especialista em soluções de produção de energia solar, reforçou a instalação fotovoltaica da empresa Veneporte com a instalação de uma bateria industrial de 200 kWh para armazenamento de energia. A instalação fotovoltaica integra 1.285 módulos fotovoltaicos de 555 W, correspondendo a uma potência instalada superior a 700 kW. De acordo com a empresa, o projeto permite evitar a emissão de cerca de 487 toneladas de CO2 por ano. Com a integração da bateria industrial para armazenamento de energia no sistema, a instalação solar passa a armazenar excedentes de energia produzida no período de almoço e aos fins de semana, evitando o seu desperdício. Além disso, a instalação da bateria possibilita a manutenção de cargas críticas em funcionamento, nomeadamente, todo o sistema informático da empresa, em caso de corte de energia a partir da rede elétrica. “O armazenamento de energia está a assumir um papel cada vez mais estratégico na gestão energética das empresas. A combinação entre produção fotovoltaica e baterias de armazenamento de energia industriais permite aproveitar ao máximo a energia produzida, reduzir custos operacionais e aumentar a resiliência energética dos negócios. É uma solução que responde não só às necessidades atuais das empresas, mas também aos desafios futuros da transição energética”, afirma Miguel Chã, Gestor de projeto da Sunenergy, em comunicado. Segundo a empresa, a aposta da Sunenergy em soluções de armazenamento acompanha a evolução do mercado e responde às necessidades de empresas que procuram maior autonomia energética, eficiência operacional e sustentabilidade. “As baterias industriais permitem não só maximizar o valor da energia produzida, como preparar as organizações para um sistema energético cada vez mais descentralizado e inteligente”, afirma a empresa em comunicado.

artigo.texto: New proposed Colleton County data center campus draws residents’ questions COLLETON COUNTY, S.C. (WCSC) — What’s going to happen if a data center development is built in Colleton County? It’s a $6 billion question that’s fueling a debate between protecting the rural environment or the potential economic boost it could bring to the county. The Colleton County Economic Alliance hosted a data center information session for local residents to answer questions about a new 1,000-megawatt data center development. “I came in prepared with about six pages of printouts with questions,” Nancy Thomas, a local resident of Colleton County, said. Residents wished this information had come sooner, just one week after the county passed its new digital infrastructure overlay district. The Rhodes Technology Park is a data center campus spanning more than 1,200 acres, with 10 data centers and two substations. “This is a single-user large hyperscale campus. We do not yet know who the user may be. You know, the Microsofts of the world, the Metas of the world, the Oracles of the world, will be a user occupying this entire facility,” Ken Loeber, a partner with Eagle Rock Partners, said. The project is west of I-95 off Mount Carmel Road, inside the new overlay district. Developers say it will meet a 65-decibel noise limit, use a closed-loop, non-evaporative cooling system and include proper buffers to mitigate impacts. “It sits behind a treed buffer because of the height of the trees. It really is $6 billion off of Mount Carmel Road that no one will be able to see,” Loeber said. Project leaders say that investment will create 500 permanent jobs and more than 1,000 construction jobs over five to seven years. “You’re talking $95 to 105,000 a year. That’s double our median household income,” Brantley Strickland, executive director of the Colleton County Economic Alliance, said. Loeber says 30% of the jobs would be network and IT engineers, about 30% would be in facility management, 30% would be in security and 10% would be administrative jobs. “We had a great meeting on Thursday of last week with some of the local contractors, people in the contracting community. And they said, ‘Look, we realize we’re not a large enough general contractor to run a $6 billion project, but I can certainly put up lights and I can certainly do other things. How do I as a Colleton County business owner or a laborer, how do I make sure that I’m prepared to be able to do that work when it occurs?’” Loeber said. A development agreement is also being finalized. It would fund road improvements near the property, create a contractor-training program so local residents can take part in construction and even invest in the future of STEM. Residents now have answers to questions about the proposed benefits. “What about a training program for local young people? They’re going to have a training program connected with the schools. That’s a plus,” Thomas said. Project leaders say the development will not cause rate increases for local residents and it is not tied to the Canady Gas Plant project. “Electric cooperatives of South Carolina have entered into an agreement that none of this transmission cost is going to be passed on to the residential customers. In fact, you may even see your residential rates go down because of that improved grid and the stability of that and sharing that fixed cost,” Strickland said. “We are paying for all the off-site transmission infrastructure as we should,” Loeber said. “The new gas plant is going to power South Carolina. We are taking power off the South Carolina grid, but there are many other ways that the grid in South Carolina is funded. We are not here because of the Canady’s plant. We didn’t follow it. It’s not being built for us,” Loeber said. And the county says the projected tax revenue from this project could be transformational. “We feel like this is our opportunity to kind of make that next step into the future and do something really great for our citizens. The ability to provide better county services; maybe people’s property taxes will even go down. We can pay teachers better, we can pay deputies better,” Strickland said. “Year four, you’re passing that $100 million a year threshold, so you know that would be huge. That’s more than doubling the county budget.” Eagle Rock Partners says, at its core, the facility’s purpose is simple. “Have electrons come in and knowledge come out. And that knowledge can be used in a host of different ways. Having that here where it’s controlled and regulated and American, I think is comforting,” Loeber said. Project leaders say construction is expected to begin around 2028 or 2029 as they finalize their energy and transmission study with Santee Cooper. Copyright 2026 WCSC. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: Dive Brief: - Energy storage systems supplied 13% to 19% of total generation at capacity factors, on par with gas-fired peaker plants when supply was at its tightest on California’s grid in 2024, avoiding more than $29 million in peak energy costs, RMI said in an analysis released earlier this month. - The following year, energy storage systems supplied 6% to 9% of generation during the Electric Reliability Council of Texas grid’s tightest hours, RMI said. - But an ERCOT rule change in December 2025 dampened energy storage systems’ ancillary services participation, adding $3.6 million to ERCOT wholesale pricing over just 24 hours and underscoring batteries’ role in maintaining cost-effective grid stability, RMI said. Dive Insight: RMI’s report lands at an uncertain time for the U.S. energy storage industry. The nonprofit energy think tank’s forecast for 30% annual growth in battery deployment over the next five years is based on a projection made by London-based energy consultancy Wood Mackenzie in 2024, when the Biden-era Inflation Reduction Act was still in full effect. Earlier this year, Wood Mackenzie dialed back its five-year forecast for utility-scale battery deployments to 16%. Wood Mackenzie’s most recent forecast, released today, sees utility-scale deployment flatlining in 2026 and growing just 8% through 2031. Analysts say President Trump’s August executive order restricting deployment of foreign-produced bulk power components layers new challenges for the industry on top of existing headwinds like import tariffs and unfavorable tax treatment of systems reliant on parts tied to China. RMI’s report finds already-deployed batteries were helping to stabilize major U.S. grids as far back as 2022. At the peak of a record-breaking heat wave that year, 3.4 GW of grid batteries met 6% of California’s energy needs and “materially strengthened the system’s ability to maintain reserve margins,” RMI said, citing an ICF analysis. During a less intense heat wave two years earlier, when it had less than 1 GW of grid-connected battery capacity, California saw rolling blackouts despite a demand peak roughly 10% lower, according to the report. RMI found utility-scale energy storage systems provide significant financial benefits to host communities as well. Its review of project agreements in California, Massachusetts, Nevada and Texas put the average annual gross tax contribution around $6,600/MW, with some contributing more than $10,000/MW. RMI said a 250 MW/500 MWh battery installation that came online in February will provide about $46 million in revenue over 20 years for the town of Medway, Massachusetts. And even after factoring in partial state property tax abatements, the 400-MW Purple Sage Energy Center will deliver $3.4 million in payments to local governments in Nevada each year, the group said. Libra, another solar-and-storage installation in Nevada, will pay $170 million in property and sales taxes over its lifetime, RMI added. RMI’s report found significant local health benefits from replacing gas-fired peaker capacity with batteries, too. RMI used the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s CO-Benefits Risk Assessment Health Impacts Screening and Mapping Tool to determine that Suffolk County, New York, could avoid $5.3 million in annual health costs by transitioning its 500-MW Port Jefferson peaker to battery storage. Harris County, Texas, could avoid $3.8 million in annual health costs by swapping its 240-MW La Porte peaker plant for batteries, according to RMI. Despite high-profile safety incidents like a January 2025 fire that destroyed most of a 300-MW Vistra energy storage array near Santa Cruz, California, serious battery fires are rare and are likely to remain that way now that the more stable lithium-iron-phosphate battery chemistry is the industry norm for stationary storage, RMI said. artigo.texto: Insight and analysis on the data center space from industry thought leaders. Enterprises Adopt Colocation for AI and Hybrid Cloud Initiatives Enterprises are strategically choosing colocation data centers to host AI applications, deploy a hybrid cloud model, add incremental capacity, improve connectivity, and reduce costs. Enterprises are increasingly choosing colocation data centers to host AI inference computing, which performs best using higher cabinet densities than are supported in most legacy corporate data centers. Modern colocation facilities support 35 kW cabinets with air cooling and 70-150 kW cabinets using optional liquid-cooling solutions. Because liquid cooling can be added once higher-density cabinets are needed, enterprise users with uncertain densification timelines can avoid stranding capital expenditures on infrastructure, making this “pay-as-you-go” model attractive. AI inference computing is highly iterative, requiring rapid, continuous interaction with large volumes of corporate financial, operational, and research data. Enterprises optimize AI inference computing performance by placing it near their other data centers to enjoy ultra-low round-trip telecom latencies. Enterprises can also install AI applications in edge colocation data centers near specialized data sources and use cases, such as factories, financial market feeds, and research labs. Colocation is available near almost every major city, but most public cloud regions operate from only a few major data center markets in each country. Colocation also offers cybersecurity advantages for AI applications. Because AI inference computing accesses valuable, confidential corporate data, many enterprises in highly regulated industries like financial services and healthcare prefer to perform inference internally in private colocation suites with dedicated network circuits and self-operated firewalls rather than sending that data off-site to third-party AI startups. Hybrid Cloud Adoption and Rebalancing Public cloud adoption remains strong: 74% of enterprises accelerated cloud migrations last year, according to Foundry’s 2026 Cloud Computing Study, seeking the flexibility, agility, and low capital investment offered by the cloud. However, prompted by rapidly escalating cloud costs and several highly publicized cloud outages, many enterprises are rethinking “cloud only” strategies by shifting to a hybrid cloud plus colocation or on-premises model. VMware’s Private Cloud Outlook 2026 indicates that 83% of enterprises have completed or are planning to repatriate workloads back from the public cloud, driven by security, cost, compliance, and performance concerns. In the push toward hybrid cloud, many enterprises now tailor workload placement to whichever delivery path works best for each specific application and data set. Enterprises often choose public cloud for dynamic capacity and cloud-native applications, but colocation and on-premises for predictable workloads and those that underperform technically or are cost-prohibitive in public cloud. Colocation also effectively hosts private clouds seeking the advantages of public cloud in a more controlled computing and security environment. Capacity Expansion Without Long Build Cycles Enterprises seek scalable data center capacity for both AI and traditional corporate computing (research, accounting, finance, sales, and legal), which is vital to all businesses. AFCOM’s 2026 State of the Data Center Report indicates that 75% of enterprises expect AI workloads to increase overall capacity requirements. Colocation offers incremental capacity expansion, allowing enterprises to increase or decrease capacity as needs change. Enterprises often prefer colocation to expanding on-premises capacity because on-premises data center construction can be expensive, time-consuming, and, in some cases, impossible due to the age of legacy facilities or physical limitations. Cost Predictability and Governance Colocation typically offers lower occupancy costs than public cloud for stable, predictable workloads. Most new colocation campuses are massive – often 50+ MW – delivering economies of scale in both upfront construction costs and operating expenses unavailable at smaller on-premises data centers. An enterprise seeking 2 MW of new capacity can occupy it at much lower cost in colocation than in a new on-premises data center. Colocation also avoids unpredictable, unbudgeted cost overages in public cloud deployments, often driven by unforeseen variable usage, opaque fees, and weak monitoring tools or practices. Enterprise users in Flexera’s 2026 State of the Cloud Report estimate that 29% of their cloud spending is wasted. Application Performance and Networking Enhancement Colocation supports legacy applications not written to be cloud-native, which often perform poorly in public cloud environments, while other corporate applications require lower telecom latency than is available from public cloud placements when corporate data centers aren’t located near cloud campuses. Some enterprises enhance connectivity for their computing portfolio using dedicated networking cabinets in interconnection-focused colocation facilities near their primary data centers. In this topology, enterprises secure competitively priced metro-area circuits from 20+ telecom carriers and cloud direct-connect circuits available in urban carrier hotels. International Operations and Data Sovereignty Many US-based multinational corporations operate their domestic data centers in-house but turn to international colocation suites for worldwide operations where data sovereignty, low-latency access to foreign operations and customers, or audit and compliance requirements necessitate local computing. International colocation providers also usually offer à la carte managed services that are valuable to enterprises without local IT staff. artigo.texto: Kochi: The severity of the present power crisis in Kerala is something the state has not faced in the past two decades. Adverse climatic conditions caused by El Nino, a spike in the use of air-conditioners and electric vehicle chargers, unavailability of power across the country and failure on the part of the state govt in implementing short-term solutions at a fast pace â all these have contributed to the current situation. It seems things will change for the better â at least for a few months until next summer. The state procured around 380MW from other states, especially from north India, during April-May 2026. Keralam recorded the highest power consumption in April this year â more than 6,100MW. Back then, the north Indian states had adequate power and less consumption. Keralam entered into a power swapping agreement with those states by assuring that electricity would be returned in the July-Sept period, when Keralam normally gets good rain and has surplus power. The northern states where the monsoon arrives much later will need more electricity in these months. In Sept, Keralamâs obligations to return power procured under power swapping will end. It means the stateâs power shortage will become less by 380MW. Similarly, the state govt is negotiating with other states to procure power to tide over the current crisis and is expecting a positive outcome. Given the fact that the shortage of power Keralam now faces is around 1,000 MW, the crisis may subside to a certain extent soon. But from March to May next year, it is almost certain that Keralam will stumble upon a severe power shortage unless the state govt takes immediate steps anticipating the crisis. âIn Sept 2025, our demand was around 4,000 MW. Now, it has increased by more than 1,000 MW due to soaring temperature and subsequent use of air-conditioners among other factors. Unlike in the past, there is a power shortage across India. So, we wonât get power even if we try to buy it,â KSEB chairperson and managing director M G Rajamanickam said. Of the total 5,51,994MW power generated in India as on July 31 this year, 1,64,595MW is solar energy. âThe total renewable energy produced in the country is more than 2 lakh MW. Of this, private generators produce around 60%. Apprehensions are being raised whether the private generators have any role in creating the shortage of power. The fact remains to be probed,â said KSEB Employees Association president Manoj E. Experts in the power sector say that Keralam must design both short-term and long-term plans to mitigate the crisis. âKSEB should prepare a resource adequacy plan with a clear vision on the next 10 yearsâ demand and supply. The board submitted its plan to us last Dec, but it was incomplete. There should be a meticulous plan for 8,765 hours in a year. For this purpose, the board should map the current availability. KSEB must prepare a least-cost capacity addition plan as well,â said Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission member B Pradeep. âKSEB and govt should ensure that the plan is being implemented as well,â he added. The total capacity of solar power plants across Keralam is around 4,500MW. The irony is that most of the solar power generated in the state is being wasted due to lack of storage facilities. KSEB has designed projects to set up a battery energy storage system (BESS) to the tune of 1,900MW. Of this, BESS facilities at Mylatti in Kasaragod (125MW) and Sreekantapuram in Kannur (40MW) may be commissioned by Jan. âWe have the potential to increase the solar energy capacity to 3,600MW-4,000MW. Several applications by consumers to set up rooftop solar plants are pending before KSEB. What we need are BESS facilities,â said energy transition consultant Sasi Kottayil. âAround 64% of solar power generated during daytime is excess. Besides KSEB setting them up, there should be community BESS facilities at panchayat level. Local bodies can set them up with the support of cooperatives. Energy can be available as cheaply as Re 1 per unit from other states during daytime. KSEB can procure that energy during daytime and store it in BESS for meeting the demand at night,â he added. According to KSEBâs projection, the gestation period (the time for setting up a facility and commissioning it) is around 18 months. But Kottayil says that a community BESS facility can be set up in a container, in three or four months. A pumped storage system is another long-term solution for which new reservoirs must be built downstream of the existing dams of hydel projects. Water flowing down from the dam after power generation could be stored in the reservoir downstream and pumped again to the dam upstream to generate power. But the gestation period of the pumped storage systems is around 8-10 years. After the mid-eighties, KSEB has not launched any major projects to generate power. âWeâve been depending on procured power to meet our needs all these years. In the absence of our own projects, power crisis may be the order of the day. Maharashtraâs demand is around 30,000MW, but it generates around 27,000MW. So, their dependency on other states is only around 10%. All south Indian states face power crises, but most of them generate a high quantity of energy on their own. But our generation is just around 25%. That means we have 75% dependency on other states. Here lies the key problem,â Rajamanickam said. âOther states have a mix of hydel, wind, solar, thermal and nuclear plants. So, if one mode of energy does not come through, they can depend on another. Setting up thermal plants in Keralam is not viable. But our potential in hydel projects is yet to be tapped fully. There should be a consensus in this regard. Similarly, the Union govt is introducing Santhi Project whereby if a state where a nuclear plant is located demands 100% energy generated from it, then it should be given. artigo.texto: O sistema de armazenamento de energia (ESS) da DoGo Power, que forma redes inteligentes, foi lançado e está pronto para encomendas globais. XANGAI, 22 de setembro de 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A DoGo Power realizou o evento "Formando o Futuro da Energia" - Estratégia e Lançamento de Novos Produtos, lançando globalmente sua estratégia "Orientada a Cenários + Formação de Redes + IA", juntamente com soluções inteligentes de armazenamento de energia para formação de redes para cenários comerciais e industriais (C&I) de grande e médio porte e em escala de serviços públicos. Robin Zhu, fundador e CEO da DoGo Power, afirmou: "Após uma rápida expansão em escala, o setor de armazenamento de energia entrou em uma fase de desenvolvimento de alta qualidade." A adaptação de cenários, a formação de redes e a IA tornaram-se elementos essenciais da competitividade. O armazenamento de energia precisa deixar de ser uma "unidade de custo" e se tornar uma "unidade criadora de valor". A DoGo Power concentra-se no armazenamento de energia em escala de rede para formação de redes elétricas, com o objetivo de ser líder em tecnologia de ponta para o novo tipo de sistema de energia. Buscamos cooperar com parceiros globais para fomentar um novo crescimento industrial através da inovação tecnológica." A DoGo Power estabeleceu três centros de P&D e dois centros de simulação e testes na China, reunindo 19 grupos de especialistas interdisciplinares liderados por doutores, com mais de 60% da equipe dedicada à P&D. Seus três centros de produção globais oferecem uma capacidade de produção de 10 GWh na primeira fase. Apoiada por uma rede de vendas e serviços que abrange mais de 30 países e regiões, a DoGo evoluiu da exportação de produtos para a operação localizada. Orientação estratégica: Da industrialização da energia renovável à transformação das indústrias tradicionais pelas energias renováveis. A DoGo Power identifica um caminho de evolução em quatro estágios para um novo tipo de sistema de energia: 1-Expansão de P&D, da indústria e das tecnologias, 2-Formação de Grade para Estabilização, 3-IA para Maior Receita e 4-Integração Inteligente Holística. O setor encontra-se atualmente na Fase 2. Com base nisso, a DoGo desenvolve uma solução para a Etapa 3 e implementa negócios globais rumo à Etapa 4 sob dois pilares principais: - Definição de soluções baseada em cenários reais de clientes, desafios práticos e valor comercial mensurável. - A plataforma tecnológica 4S, desenvolvida internamente, impulsionada duplamente pela formação de redes e pela IA, possibilita um sistema de energia definido por algoritmo. Integrando EMS, PMS, PCS e BMS, a plataforma 4S constrói estações de armazenamento de energia inteligentes capazes de análise, otimização, tomada de decisões e atualização iterativa. Com o respaldo dessa base técnica, a DoGo fornece soluções em escala de rede adequadas para diversos cenários, requisitos de múltiplas energias e múltiplas escalas temporais em todo o mundo. Soluções de Novos Produtos Baseadas em Cenários Duas soluções emblemáticas de sistemas de armazenamento de energia (ESS) para formação de redes inteligentes foram lançadas para cenários comerciais e industriais (C&I) e de grande escala para concessionárias de serviços públicos. 1.Solução C&I Smart GFM ESS Adotando um design compacto do tipo "1 ESS substitui 8 gabinetes", esta unidade de 3 metros consolida as funções de seis gabinetes ESS de 260 kWh+, um gabinete combinador, um gabinete on/off-grid e um transformador de isolamento. Isso reduz o CAPEX inicial em 1,2 centavos de dólar por Wh, diminui a ocupação de terras em 35% e encurta a entrega do projeto em 5 a 7 dias. Com suporte para acesso a múltiplas fontes, como painéis fotovoltaicos, geradores a diesel, pontos de recarga, rede elétrica e sistemas de gerenciamento, o sistema permite a comutação perfeita entre conexão e desconexão da rede em ≤20ms, atendendo de forma confiável cargas sensíveis e de alta potência e concretizando o conceito de "1 contêiner equivale a 1 microrrede". A capacidade de dimensionamento flexível suporta a implantação mista de diferentes séries e a compatibilidade com inversores de terceiros para maximizar a utilização dos ativos existentes. 2.Solução de armazenamento de energia GFM inteligente em escala de utilidade pública Desenvolvido para projetos com terrenos complexos e restrições de transporte, o contêiner pesa menos de 22 toneladas, dobrando as rotas de transporte viáveis em comparação com os contêineres convencionais de 20 pés e reduzindo os custos de logística marítima e terrestre. Seu design sem cabos elimina a necessidade de escavações e montagem de cabos no local, com o pré-comissionamento completo do sistema realizado na fábrica. Aproveitando a arquitetura dinâmica de taxa C, os clientes podem começar com uma implementação de duração de 2 horas para controlar o CAPEX e expandir por meio de gabinetes de expansão de data center para ajustar suavemente as taxas C e as durações de backup para corresponder aos modelos de negócios em evolução. artigo.texto: A infraestrutura para inteligência artificial ganhou destaque nos programas de governo de importantes nomes da política nacional. Figuras como Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema e Renan Santos concordam sobre a urgência de ampliar a capacidade computacional, embora apresentem visões distintas sobre o papel estatal, incentivos e regras ambientais. Diferenças nas propostas dos candidatos As estratégias variam conforme o grupo político. O plano de Lula vincula os servidores à autonomia tecnológica, sugerindo supercomputadores e serviços de nuvem controlados por instituições brasileiras, além de impor critérios rigorosos de eficiência energética e uso de recursos hídricos. Por outro lado, Ronaldo Caiado condiciona benefícios tributários a metas socioambientais e tecnológicas. Já Flávio Bolsonaro e Romeu Zema focam na captação de recursos privados, priorizando energia acessível e desregulamentação para atrair as empresas. Enquanto Renan Santos aposta em zonas econômicas voltadas à inovação, Augusto Cury enxerga a tecnologia como um pilar estratégico de Estado, embora sem detalhar medidas específicas para a instalação dessas estruturas físicas. Desafios na busca por autonomia digital Especialistas apontam que a simples multiplicação de servidores no território nacional não assegura autonomia. “Você pode ser um quintal para data centers de outros, que simplesmente vão absorver os seus recursos naturais e energéticos”, afirma Luca Belli, professor da Fundação Getulio Vargas. Para o meio acadêmico, o ideal seria envolver universidades, centros de pesquisa e governos locais no processo. Além disso, existe uma forte dependência externa em relação a fornecedores de chips avançados e serviços de computação em nuvem, dominados por poucas corporações estrangeiras. Impactos na infraestrutura e o avanço do Redata O consumo massivo de eletricidade e água para refrigeração e funcionamento contínuo dessas instalações preocupa entidades de defesa do consumidor, como o Idec, que cobra rigor nas regras de localização e estudos de impacto. Enquanto o debate político ocorre, o Congresso já movimenta pautas econômicas para o setor. O Senado aprovou recentemente o Redata, programa que concede isenções bilionárias de tributos como IPI, PIS/Cofins e imposto de importação para o setor, exigindo em contrapartida o uso de energia limpa e eficiência hídrica. O cenário internacional também impõe desafios geopolíticos complexos para o país, dividindo atenções entre potências globais. Sobre esse aspecto, a ministra da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação, Luciana Santos, pontuou em entrevista à Folha de S.Paulo: “Os Estados Unidos ameaçam cessar o fornecimento a quem fizer negócios nessas áreas mais críticas com a China.” Dessa forma, o futuro digital brasileiro depende não apenas do volume de investimentos atraídos, mas da capacidade de reter tecnologia, gerar empregos qualificados e proteger os recursos naturais essenciais para a população.

artigo.texto: Report finds Oregon data centers used electricity equal to over 70% of all homes in state PORTLAND Ore. (KPTV) - Researchers from ECOnorthwest and the University of Virginia have released a new report on data centers in Oregon. According to the report, there are 111 data centers in the state, and those consumed more than 14 terawatt-hours of electricity last year. That’s equal to about 71% of all the electricity sold to Oregon homes combined. Meanwhile, consumption has nearly quadrupled since 2020. By 2030, researchers say data centers could account for roughly one-third of Oregon’s entire electricity demand. The report says 32 more data centers are already planned or under construction across the state, adding even more strain to the grid. Researchers say Oregon’s energy system will need new generation and transmission infrastructure to keep up with the growth. Copyright 2026 KPTV-KPDX. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: Google files request for 200+ additional emergency generators at Fort Wayne data center IDEM approved 140 backup generators for the project earlier this year FORT WAYNE, Ind. (WPTA) - Google announced on Monday morning that it has submitted a request to the Indiana Department of Environmental Management to add more than 200 additional emergency generators to its Fort Wayne data center. The tech giant has sent in a third air permit modification application to the Indiana Department of Environmental Management to add 228 emergency generators. In April, IDEM approved a request to add more than 140 emergency diesel generators to the data center campus following public pushback. That approval also included five smaller generators classified as “insignificant” by state law. Those generators joined the 34 main diesel generators that IDEM first greenlit for the project back in 2024. A Google spokesperson said in its latest request that the additional 228 backup generators will be used only as a safety net if the local power grid goes down. They say aside from outages, the units will also run during legally required maintenance checks, and anticipate less than 10 hours of testing per generator annually. The EPA-certified emergency generators use ultra-low sulfur diesel or renewable diesel alternatives like Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil (HVO), Google says. The company says that even if the new request is approved, the site will remain below its state-mandated emissions cap. Google also says it has installed air pollution controls on several generators, which will modify units to ensure they meet or exceed EPA Tier 4 emission standards. Currently, there is no information on IDEM’s website that indicates that a public hearing will be held on the request. 21Alive News has reached out to the department for further clarification. Earlier this month, the department approved developers’ request to fill just over two acres of wetlands. In September of last year, IDEM approved a similar request to fill more than two acres of wetlands in an earlier expansion phase. artigo.texto: Nova Scotia Power has inaugurated three 50MW/200MWh battery energy storage systems (BESS) in Bridgewater, Waverley and White Rock, now Atlantic Canada’s largest battery storage facilities. The Government of Canada invested CA$109 million (US$79 million) for pre-development work, installation and grid modernisation upgrades tied to the projects, part of Natural Resources Canada’s Electricity Predevelopment Program. The Canada Infrastructure Bank (CIB), a federal Crown corporation that provides debt financing for infrastructure projects, provided a further CA$138.2 million loan. Nova Scotia Power, the province’s monopoly electric utility, expects the combined 150MW/600MWh portfolio to support the province’s shift away from coal-fired generation and strengthen grid reliability during peak-demand periods and outages. The Canada Infrastructure Bank said the arrangement marks the first clean energy project backed by its Indigenous Equity Initiative. Vivek Sood, president and CEO of Nova Scotia Power, said the completion of all three sites reflected years of planning, engineering and community engagement. “These projects strengthen the reliability of the electricity system for our customers while enabling the continued growth of renewable energy across the province,” Sood said. Crystal Nicholas, president and general manager of the WMA, said the equity structure gives Mi’kmaw communities a direct stake in the province’s energy transition. “Inclusion in such projects opens pathways toward economic reconciliation and ensures that traditional Indigenous values are considered in major project development,” Nicholas said. Nova Scotia Utility and Review Board regulators approved the three-site portfolio in 2024, following amendments the province made to its Electricity Act in 2023 specifically to accelerate energy storage deployment. Those amendments allowed Nova Scotia Power to run competitive solicitations to procure battery storage resources, a legislative change that paved the way for the Bridgewater, Waverley and White Rock sites to proceed to construction. Nova Scotia has estimated it will need between 300MW and 400MW of energy storage by 2030 to help meet its target of 80% renewable energy and a full coal phase-out by that date. In 2022, more than 70% of the province’s electricity still came from coal, natural gas and other fossil fuels, with renewables, including hydro, wind, tidal and solar, contributing around 23%. Nova Scotia already hosts more than 300 commercial wind turbines, including five wind farms that are majority-owned by Mi’kmaw communities, and Chinese wind turbine manufacturer Envision Energy has separately signed a partnership agreement to explore a 300MW hybrid wind-plus-storage project near Sydney, Nova Scotia. Provincial utilities across Canada are moving on battery storage through different procurement models Nova Scotia’s approach, a utility-led build supported by direct federal investment and an Indigenous equity structure, sits alongside distinct battery storage strategies emerging in other provinces. In Ontario, the Independent Electricity System Operator’s (IESO) Long-Term 1 and Long-Term 2 procurement rounds have driven the country’s largest battery contracting activity to date, including the 250MW/1,000MWh Napanee BESS, developed by a joint venture between Ameresco and Atura Power, which began commercial operations in May 2026 roughly five weeks ahead of schedule and under its CA$600 million budget. Ontario’s storage build-out has been driven partly by the scheduled 2026 closure of the 2,100MW Pickering Nuclear station. Trade association Energy Storage Canada has recommended the province establish a dedicated procurement track for behind-the-meter and distribution-connected battery storage, arguing that existing compensation structures undervalue the grid services smaller, faster-to-deploy battery assets can already provide. British Columbia is taking a more centralised approach. BC Hydro, the province’s Crown-owned utility, is advancing what it describes as the first major battery storage project in the province, a facility of at least 100MW planned for a site near Duncan on Vancouver Island, which the utility intends to own and operate directly rather than procure through a long-term contract with a private developer. BC Hydro has identified up to 500MW of potential battery storage capacity across the province under its Powering Growth plan. Federally, the Nova Scotia investment is part of the government’s broader CA$4.5 billion Smart Renewables and Electrification Pathways Program, which supports grid modernisation, storage and renewables deployment across every Canadian region, and follows the government’s May 2026 launch of a national strategy aimed at doubling the country’s grid capacity by 2050.

artigo.texto: E.ON and BYD have entered into a strategic partnership to expand intelligent energy and electric mobility solutions for customers across Europe, with the first joint offering scheduled to launch in Germany in November 2026. Under the partnership, E.ON will contribute its expertise in energy supply, smart charging and flexibility management, while BYD will provide its expertise in electric vehicles and battery technologies. The companies plan to gradually extend the joint offering to additional European markets. The partnership comes as the European electric mobility market continues to expand. Around 10–11 million battery-electric vehicles are currently on European roads, with the number potentially reaching 40–50 million by 2030. The companies said this growth is increasing the need to integrate electric vehicles more closely with the energy system. Under the planned offering, customers purchasing or leasing a fully electric BYD vehicle will have access to compatible energy and charging solutions from E.ON. Existing E.ON customers will also be able to benefit from the joint solutions. First Joint Offering to Launch in Germany E.ON and BYD will introduce their first joint customer offering in Germany in November 2026. The package will combine the purchase or leasing of a fully electric BYD vehicle with a smart electricity contract from E.ON and is planned to be available across BYD’s fully electric model range. Customers leasing a vehicle could reduce their monthly costs by up to €20 through the use of intelligent charging functions. E.ON will optimize the charging process automatically, while a dedicated bonus scheme will reward customers for flexible electricity consumption. The companies plan to expand the offering to other European markets in subsequent phases while continuing to develop the digital customer experience. Planned initiatives include integrating services into mobile applications and exploring technologies such as mixed reality to assist customers with vehicle setup and commissioning. BYD Vehicles to Integrate With E.ON Home Energy Platform E.ON’s existing E.ON Home Comfort platform connects and manages energy assets such as wallboxes, battery storage systems and heat pumps. The platform is designed to optimize household energy flows and enable customers to benefit from flexible energy consumption. As part of the partnership, BYD electric vehicles will be gradually integrated into the E.ON Home Comfort platform. This will enable customers to manage their vehicles, smart charging functions and, over time, other home energy solutions through a single digital environment. The companies said customers will retain control over their data and how it is used. Partnership Targets Bidirectional Charging E.ON and BYD also plan to test and scale additional flexibility solutions, including bidirectional charging and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology. V2G enables electric vehicles to function as flexible energy storage assets by allowing electricity to flow between the vehicle and the grid. The companies said wider adoption of the technology could support the integration of renewable energy, reduce overall energy system costs and create additional savings opportunities for customers. Marc Spieker, Chief Operating Officer Commercial at E.ON SE, said the partnership combines energy, mobility and digital technologies while creating a foundation for bringing flexibility services such as bidirectional charging to the mass market. Patrick Schulz, Deputy Country Manager and Commercial Director of BYD Germany, said the partnership aims to simplify the transition to electric mobility by combining BYD’s electric vehicle and battery technology with E.ON’s energy solutions.

artigo.texto: Aprovação de regras para data centers deve destravar investimentos no RN A aprovação, pelo Conselho Estadual do Meio Ambiente (Conema), de regras para a instalação de data centers vai ajudar a destravar investimentos, gerar emprego e renda, além de trazer segurança jurídica para o Rio Grande do Norte A aprovação, pelo Conselho Estadual do Meio Ambiente (Conema), de regras para a instalação de data centers vai ajudar a destravar investimentos, gerar emprego e renda, além de trazer segurança jurídica para o Rio Grande do Norte. É o que avaliam segmentos que representam a indústria de energias renováveis do estado ouvidos pela TRIBUNA DO NORTE. A minuta de resolução deve ser publicada no Diário Oficial do Estado ainda esta semana. O documento aprovado pelo conselho na última segunda-feira (21) estabelece diretrizes, critérios e procedimentos para o licenciamento ambiental dos data centers no RN. A medida cria, pela primeira vez, um regramento específico para a atividade, permitindo ao Instituto de Desenvolvimento Sustentável e Meio Ambiente do RN (Idema) iniciar o licenciamento de projetos. Darlan Santos, presidente do Centro de Estratégias em Recursos Naturais e Energia (Cerne), avalia que a aprovação da minuta “é um passo decisivo, necessário e positivo”, sendo a previsibilidade regulatória o principal ativo para atração de investimentos. “A clara diferenciação entre sistemas de refrigeração fechados e abertos demonstra maturidade técnica na análise socioambiental, indicando a preocupação dos recursos hídricos do estado, enquanto desburocratiza projetos de menor impacto hídrico por meio do Relatório Ambiental Simplificado”, diz. Segundo Williman Oliveira, presidente da Associação Potiguar de Energias Renováveis (APER), a medida vai acelerar as discussões em torno do tema e ajudar a gerar emprego e renda no estado. “Temos urgentemente que oferecer essa oportunidade aos investidores, uma vez que tivermos com as normas e leis que tragam a segurança jurídica para os investimentos”, disse. A resolução representa um avanço, mas, ainda assim, cercado de desafios, na avaliação do presidente da APER. “É preciso prestar a infraestrutura em paralelo à legislação favorável para o desenvolvimento de data centers do RN, o que é um desafio”, explica. O presidente da Federação das Indústrias do RN, Roberto Serquiz, disse reconhecer a posição do Governo do Estado, “que compreendeu a importância dessa agenda e fez valer a qualidade técnica do órgão ambiental, com a participação decisiva dos diretores e secretários ligados ao desenvolvimento sustentável”. Segundo Roberto Serquiz, a resolução avançou mesmo diante da resistência de setores que historicamente se recusam a reconhecer que é possível e necessário aliar proteção ambiental e desenvolvimento. “Agora torcemos para que nossos parlamentares também avancem na aprovação da Política Ambiental que está em pauta, incorporando esses conceitos e ajudando o RN a recuperar sua capacidade competitiva”, falou. Empreendimentos serão classificados em categorias De acordo com o Idema, a resolução cria uma regulamentação estadual para a atividade e padroniza os procedimentos administrativos, técnicos e ambientais aplicáveis aos empreendimentos. Os data centers são instalações destinadas ao processamento, armazenamento e comunicação de dados, reunindo estruturas como fornecimento de energia, refrigeração, segurança, conectividade e servidores, além da infraestrutura de distribuição de energia. Um dos principais critérios para o enquadramento dos projetos será a capacidade elétrica instalada. Os empreendimentos serão classificados em cinco categorias: micro, com até 20 MW; pequeno, acima de 20 MW até 50 MW; médio, acima de 50 MW até 100 MW; grande, acima de 100 MW até 500 MW; e excepcional, acima de 500 MW. A potência considerada inclui os equipamentos de tecnologia da informação e os sistemas de refrigeração. A modalidade de licenciamento e os estudos ambientais exigidos também devem variar conforme o porte e o sistema de refrigeração adotado. Nos sistemas fechados, a água utilizada no resfriamento dos equipamentos circula dentro de um circuito e é reaproveitada, sem necessidade de reposição constante em grandes volumes. Já os sistemas abertos, que utilizam torres de refrigeração, podem resultar em consumo hídrico maior. Segundo o diretor-geral do Idema, Werner Farkatt, a proposta foi amplamente discutida com o objetivo de garantir segurança jurídica, técnica e ambiental ao licenciamento da atividade. “Um dos principais pontos de atenção foi a diferenciação entre sistemas fechados e abertos de refrigeração, especialmente em relação ao consumo de água e à escassez hídrica no semiárido”, disse. “A resolução estabelece um licenciamento mais simplificado para sistemas fechados, enquanto os empreendimentos de grande e excepcional porte e com sistemas abertos estarão sujeitos a estudos ambientais mais complexos. A aprovação pelo Conema fortalece a segurança jurídica e cria condições para análise dos processos sem comprometer a proteção ambiental”, considerou Werner Farkatt, em seguida. O presidente Darlan Santos, do Cerne, explicou que esses empreendimentos podem estimular a hibridização de parques, com projetos que combinam eólica e solar no mesmo ponto de conexão para mitigar a variabilidade ao longo das 24 horas do dia; atrair investimentos em baterias de grande porte (Sistema de Armazenamento de Energia em Baterias, ou BESS, na sigla em inglês); e reduzir o impacto do curtailment (cortes de geração impostos ao setor renovável). artigo.texto: Elevated Materials receives $50 million from DOE for battery manufacturing The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) has selected battery component developer Elevated Materials for federal funding, granting the Californian firm $50 million to support the development of a new facility on American shores. Elevated Materials representatives say the new facility will have an annual manufacturing capacity of about 3.5 GW, with the firm producing ultra-thin lithium films for next-generation battery products. With a total price tag of $100 million, the funding will fund about half of the facility’s total construction and early operations. The new facility is expected to accelerate Elevated Materials’ path to achieving gigawatt-hour-scale for both production and commercialization of its products. The firm aims to create a new domestic source of ultra-thin lithium-metal films and prelithiated materials, in turn enabling higher energy batteries that charge faster than ever. “The United States has made advanced battery manufacturing a national priority, and securing a domestic supply of critical materials that significantly increases energy density is central to that effort,” says Elevated Materials CEO Jim Cushing. “We developed this technology in California with support from DOE R&D programs and are proud to have been selected by the Department of Energy to now ramp it up to giga-watt scale.” Bringing the next generation to the U.S. market Elevated Materials was among a group of seven companies that the DOE chose for a combined $500 million in funding. As the federal agency aims to strengthen domestic battery manufacturing and reduce reliance on international supply chains, the department’s Battery Materials Processing and Battery Manufacturing Grants program has become a high priority. The new facility will be a core part of the U.S.’s battery production supply chain going forward, according to officials from Elevated Materials officials. The firm’s roll-to-roll vacuum deposition platforms will manufacture its ELi brand of ultra-thin lithium metal films. From there, the ELi products will enable “next-generation anode architectures” across a number of markets, including grid-scale energy storage, EVs, consumer electronics, and defense applications. “Demand has been particularly strong for lithium metal anodes, where ELi significantly improves both safety and performance,” the company says in a recent news release. “Over the past year, Elevated has achieved record output of ultra-thin lithium metal films, shipping over 250,000 meters of material to more than 30 customers worldwide.”

artigo.texto: U.S. energy storage market posts record number in Q2 2026, report says Data analysis firm Wood Mackenzie has good news for the American energy storage sector in its latest U.S. Energy Storage Monitor report, as the market installed a record 18.9 GWh in Q2 2026. Even as installed power fell 7% year over year, Wood Mackenzie’s research finds that longer duration storage in utility-scale and residential storage systems drove the sector further than ever. The wattage itself went down slightly, as the company’s research notes, but wattage-hours exploded, up 17% year over year from Q2 2025. In a practical sense, that means the national average’s energy storage duration went from 2.8 hours to 3.5 hours thanks to installations from Q2 2026. “Battery storage is one of the most important tools we have to meet growing electricity demand,” says John Hensley, SVP of markets and policy analysis at American Clean Power. “Storage can be deployed quickly, strengthens reliability, and helps the grid make better use of both existing and new generation. With a strong pipeline and continued technology improvements, the outlook for storage remains exceptionally strong.” The implications of this data are far-reaching across the American energy industry, Wood Mackenzie officials say. Storage has become a trend in the solar and energy sector over the past few years. Now, that trend has its guiding star: AI data centers. “Data center buildout strengthens the U.S. storage outlook across all sectors. Storage can provide needed capacity faster, cheaper and more reliably than gas alone,” says Allison Feeney, research analyst at Wood Mackenzie. “As hyperscalers increasingly face grid-connection bottlenecks, utility-scale storage will enable speed to power for data centers.” As data centers continue to drive the storage market forward, the numbers tell a promising story for 2026. By the numbers Much of the AI data center-related came from the American utility-scale storage segment, according to Wood Mackenzie’s data. Comparing Q2 2025 to Q2 2026, the segment went down in pure wattage, installing just under 4.7 GW in Q2 2026 — good for an 8% drop in installation. However, the wattage-hours of the utility-scale segment moved up 16% from 2025 to 2026, as the segment installed more than 17.6 GWh in Q2 2026. The commercial and industrial sector of the storage market remained largely stagnant year over year, Wood Mackenzie’s data says. The segment remained practically unchanged, installing 49 MW in Q2 2025 and 48 MW in Q2 2026. Additionally, the wattage-hour numbers stayed consistent, going from 104 MWh in Q2 2025, to 103 MWh in Q2 2026. But perhaps the most promising figure from the storage segment in Q2 2026 was the residential segment. Looking at the year over year numbers, Wood Mackenzie’s research states that the residential storage market was the only segment of the three to see an uptick in wattage itself, installing 676 MW for a 3% increase over Q2 2025. The biggest swing in favor of the residential storage segment came from wattage-hour installation, Wood Mackenzie says. Going from 791 MW installed in Q2 2025, to nearly 1.2 GW in Q2 2026, the sector saw a 48% increase year over year. A promising forecast Looking forward, Wood Mackenzie representatives estimate that the American solar market will reach 207 GW / 715 GWh by 2031. Thanks to continued utility electrification, data center buildout, and the potential reinstatement of the Biden-era Solar For All program, the market is well-positioned for growth through the end of the decade. With a 21% jump in wattage-hour installation from 2025 to 2026, the market should continue to expand as it enables large load growth, the data company states. While the utility-scale sector could stagnate in 2027 as it adjusts to new supply chain dynamics, 2028 and beyond is expected to be a growth period for the market as a whole. Additionally, the market is receiving some help from an unexpected source: electric vehicles. “The slowdown in EV demand has become an unexpected tailwind for storage,” says Allison Weis, Wood Mackenzie’s global head of energy storage. “Manufacturers are repurposing idle EV cell capacity, accelerating the domestic supply base just as trade policy makes it most valuable.” In total, Wood Mackenzie officials say the U.S. energy storage market could add more than 130 GW / 534 GWh, in the utility-scale segment alone, between 2026 and 2031. The commercial and industrial segment is equally rosy with an expectation of 29% growth between 2026 and 2031. While the national residential storage market will likely drop slightly before the end of the 2026, that downgrade represents a mild hiccup in an otherwise bullish prediction.

artigo.texto: The lithium battery fire was reported around 11:40 a.m. near a solar panel field on the northeast side of the facility in the 3200 block of Wheeler Avenue. Crews from the La Verne Fire Department and Los Angeles County Fire Department responded. One employee suffered minor injuries and was taken to a local hospital, according to La Verne Fire Department Battalion Chief Mark Savage. Shortly after 3 p.m., the L.A. County Fire Department said the fire had been knocked down. AIR7 video shows firefighters dousing the flames with water. La Verne fire crews were still monitoring the scene and mopping up, noting that there was still a risk, with more lithium batteries at the site. By Tuesday evening, no flare-ups had been reported, and crews were using a drone to monitor the batteries. Firefighters estimate there are fewer than 20 lithium batteries in the storage facility. "These things do not like any kind of additional heat, and the understanding is, there is something going on with that bank now that it is reacting to the previous heat that it was exposed to," said Batt. Chief Mark Savage. "So we are monitoring closely. We have reinitiated cooling measures for that battery bank now. But it's one of those things that, once it gets started, it's extremely difficult to stop, if not impossible to stop." The fire prompted evacuation orders and warnings near Bonita Avenue and Wheeler Avenue and a shelter-in-place for the surrounding residential neighborhood. Click here to see if you are in an impacted area. Some evacuation orders were later downgraded to warnings. By early Tuesday evening, firefighters said the orders were only impacting the approximately 185 properties closest to the facility. La Verne police said shopping centers along Wheeler Avenue north of Foothill Boulevard were evacuated as a precaution. Grace Miller Elementary School, located just east of the facility, was under a shelter-in-place order, and Holly Oak Street south of the campus was closed to traffic. Savage said students appeared to be released from the school while firefighters battled the blaze. Parents told Eyewitness News that Ramona Middle School and Bonita High School were also affected. Holy Name of Mary School, Damien High School and the University of La Verne were evacuated. The university said all classes were canceled until further notice. Eyewitness News spoke to Ramona Middle School parents who arrived to pick up their kids. By the time most parents arrived, it was already the school's normal pick-up time. "They're blocking off Wheeler, so it makes it a little hectic but scary at the same time, so we're just here getting the kids out of safety," said parent Irene Flores. "We got it on our phones, the emergency message to evacuate our facility. So might as well come get the kids, make sure they're safe," said parent Jason Wagner. "In La Verne, we've never seen these kind of things." The Metropolitan Water District said its water supply was not affected by the fire. The cause of the fire is still under investigation. Savage said nothing like this has happened there before, but it's raising concerns for neighbors who had no clue that the water treatment plant housed massive battery banks with the potential to catch fire. If you're wondering if you live near a facility that houses potentially dangerous or hazardous items, you can find out. Back in May, 7 On Your Side did an investigation and we shared the Environmental Protection Agency's interactive map, where you can learn about the enforcement and compliance history of facilities near you. City News Service contributed to this report.

artigo.texto: A Eveo, empresa de servidores dedicados e private Cloud, afirmou que vive em 2026 o melhor momento da sua operação no Nordeste. O volume de novos negócios na região supera o registrado no mesmo período de 2025, e a base de clientes local cresceu 62% no último ano. Desde o início da operação regional, em 2024, essa base se multiplicou, com avanço acumulado de 272%. O movimento sustenta o plano da companhia de atingir R$ 500 milhões em receita até 2030. O crescimento é impulsionado pela demanda por servidores dedicados, private cCoud e GPU dedicada para projetos de Inteligência Artificial, com empresas da região buscando operações locais, capazes de reduzir latência e aumentar a disponibilidade de aplicações de missão crítica. Fortaleza tem papel central nessa estratégia. Segundo dados da BBC e da TeleGeography, cerca de 90% do tráfego internacional de Internet que chega ao Brasil passa pela Praia do Futuro, na capital cearense, por meio de 16 cabos submarinos que conectam o país à Europa, aos Estados Unidos, ao Caribe e à África, o que torna a cidade o principal hub de conectividade da América Latina. A Eveo opera um Data Center Tier III em Fortaleza desde 2024, e a decisão de ocupar uma nova unidade em Recife responde à alta demanda de uma região que segue carente de infraestrutura local. As distâncias no Nordeste são continentais: Recife (PE) fica a cerca de 800 quilômetros de Fortaleza, aproximadamente dez horas de carro, o que inviabiliza atender toda a região a partir de um único ponto, especialmente para aplicações sensíveis à latência. Com o novo Data Center Tier III, que será inaugurado em breve em Recife, a companhia passa a cobrir os dois principais polos do Nordeste e amplia sua capacidade de entregar servidores dedicados, private Cloud e GPU dedicada com serviços de missão crítica e preços competitivos, mais próximos de quem os utiliza. “A localização da infraestrutura vai além de uma decisão técnica. É um fator estratégico para o negócio. Estar em Fortaleza e, a partir de agora, também em Recife nos permite oferecer menor latência, maior disponibilidade e uma experiência muito mais consistente para os clientes de todo o Nordeste. Estamos crescendo na região em ritmo superior ao do ano passado, e o novo data center chega para sustentar a próxima etapa dessa expansão rumo à meta de R$ 500 milhões em receita até 2030”, afirma José Henrique Bermejo, CRO da Eveo. A expansão também se reflete na presença física da companhia. Após inaugurar, em 2025, o primeiro escritório regional fora de São Paulo, em João Pessoa (PB), a Eveo transferiu a unidade, em julho de 2026, para o edifício DCT, um dos empreendimentos corporativos mais imponentes da capital paraibana, acompanhando o crescimento da equipe local. O movimento aproxima o atendimento dos clientes e prepara a estrutura para sustentar o avanço de servidores dedicados, private Cloud e GPU dedicada em todos os estados da região. Limited (CATL) World's largest battery manufacturer Several large-scale battery energy storage system developments across Central and Eastern Europe have reached completion, financing or supplier milestones, according to Energy-Storage.news. The activity spans Romania, Bulgaria, Hungary and Poland and involves companies including Greenvolt, Renovatio, CATL, Renalfa, MOL Group, Tavion, MetaWealth, Enexus and Longi. The announcements arrive shortly before the Energy Storage Summit Central and Eastern Europe 2026, scheduled for 6-7 October in Warsaw, Poland. Construction is underway on a 918MWh battery energy storage project in Romania, described as one of the country's largest. Independent power producer Greenvolt owns the project, Renovatio Solar is providing engineering, procurement and construction services, and CATL is supplying the battery technology. The project is expected to be completed within 12 months. Developer and EPC firm Enexus will deploy 50MWh of battery storage from solar photovoltaic manufacturer Longi across two solar-plus-storage projects in Romania. The two battery projects, sized at 15MWh and 35MWh, are located in Dambovita County and represent the first storage collaboration between the companies, which have previously worked together on solar PV projects. Longi entered the battery storage sector recently through its acquisition of system integrator PotisEdge late last year. Real estate investment platform MetaWealth has completed a EUR19 million financing structure for its first battery storage project, a 50MW/100MWh facility also in Romania. The structure comprises EUR10 million from CEC bank, EUR5.5 million from the founding Topolinski family and EUR3.5 million from its securitisation and bond platform. Renalfa IPP has completed the repowering and hybridisation of its Devnya PV plant in Northeastern Bulgaria. The company increased the plant's capacity from 5MWp to 65MWp and added a battery storage system totalling 60MW/165MWh. Solarpro served as the EPC contractor. According to a speaker at the Energy Storage Summit Central and Eastern Europe, Bulgaria is now the most battery-heavy electricity market in the world. Industrial firm MOL Group has completed a 37.4MWp solar and 20MW/40MWh battery storage project in Hungary called Algyo. According to head of communications Ambrus Halasz, the project benefited from funds under Hungary's EU-backed capital expenditure grant scheme for storage. Battery storage owner-operator Tavion has raised EUR50 million, equivalent to US$57 million, through a fundraise and debt raise. The proceeds will go towards completing three projects in Poland with a combined capacity of 69MW. Leitmotif and Oberon Capital led the fundraise, which totalled EUR34 million. Construction will start on the first two projects this month. They form part of a 184MW portfolio Tavion intends to deploy in Poland.
